process_observations.observation: The declared build-scoped test did what it was declared to do. Run at --manifest-dir artefacts it reported 'Scanned 6 metadata file(s): 2 record type(s), 2 layout(s)' - both halves of the M1 pair present - while the same checker at --manifest-dir artefacts/M1-S02 reports '0 record type(s), 2 layout(s)', which is the blind half-view the plan's test description predicted word for word. The planner's scope reasoning held at run time.

M1-S01's deploy-order.md section 2 already named this step's layouts as a downstream dependency and named the milestone-scoped checker as the thing that only becomes real once both step directories exist. The two notes agree without anyone reconciling them.

The declared checker exited 0 - which is what the test asserts - but printed 2 INFO findings ('layout marks no field behavior=Required') where the planner's fixture run recorded '0 finding(s) detected'. The fixture layouts evidently carried at least one Required item and these do not. The divergence is a real design difference, not a regression: marking any Opportunity field Required on the layout is precisely what references/gotchas.md #13 forbids without a dry run, and Q11 puts the must-fill enforcement in the M2-S03/M2-S04 validation rules. No field was marked Required to make a cosmetic string match an INFO-level fixture note.

Both layout files are byte-for-byte identical; they differ only in file name. admin/record-types-and-page-layouts lists 'record type with an identical page layout to another record type' as a merge candidate to surface proactively (SKILL.md, Proactive Triggers; llm-anti-patterns.md Anti-Pattern 3, the 1:1 layout-per-record-type mapping). Nothing in the step's inputs, in Q14 or in Q20 differentiates the two field sets, so the second layout exists because decision D2 produced two record types, not because anyone asked for a different page. It is defensible - it leaves room for the motions to diverge later without a record-type change - but it should be a decision someone signs, and it is carried as item 4 of deploy-order.md section 3.

A cited skill supplied nothing writable. admin/products-and-pricebooks carries no fenced XML anywhere (the Step 3 grep returns no path), no Questions to Ask Before Configuring table, and no mention of a page layout or a related list in any of its files. It is cited for the product-line half of Q14 ('the products related list is on both'), which is exactly the element this step cannot write, and the instruction that resolved it came from admin/opportunity-management instead.

Both layouts ship incomplete against requirement item 2: with no relatedLists block, a deployed Enterprise layout shows no Opportunity Products related list, so a rep cannot add a product line from the page. The gap is deliberate (A26) and the retrieve instruction is section 0 of the deploy-order note, but a reader who takes 'the M1 layouts are built' as 'reps can add products' will be wrong, in the same shape as M1-S01's open item O-M1S01-03.

Assumption A25 and the step's manual acceptance test both name 'scripts/mock_deploy.py --dry-run', and that flag does not exist. The script's --help states it is validation-only, always runs sf project deploy start --dry-run (checkOnly), and that 'there is no flag to disable --dry-run and no --deploy option; that is by design'. Written into deploy-order.md as the runnable form - python3 scripts/mock_deploy.py <plan> --org-alias <alias> --step M1-S02 - with an explicit sentence that the --dry-run in A25's wording is the behaviour and not a flag, so the human ticking the manual test can match the two.

agents/metadata-builder/AGENT.md Step 3's gap rule says it fires 'on one condition only: the grep in item 2 returned no path at all'. admin/products-and-pricebooks meets that condition exactly, so a literal reading blocks this step with skill-gap. It was not blocked, because the rule's own blocked-exit message must name 'the metadata type and the specific elements the step needed' and this skill was needed for no element - the tell that the rule was written for a skill that owns a type the step emits, not for a skill cited as context. The judgement is recorded rather than hidden; a reviewer who disagrees should read this observation, not the artefacts.

Q19 gives the profile matrix (Sales User for reps and managers, System Administrator for sales ops, the manager distinction by role rather than profile) and it determines nothing in this step - a Layout file carries no profile reference. It determines M2-S02's Profile file entirely. Recorded here so the M1 gate does not read 'the layouts are built' as 'the right people see them'; nobody is assigned to either layout until M2-S02, which is human-gated.

decision_record.question: record-types-and-page-layouts: 'Is a field being marked Required on the layout meant to be enforced everywhere?'
decision_record.answer: No. Q11 splits the per-stage fields into must-fill and shown-for-context, and the must-fill half is a validation-rule backlog (M2-S03 Opportunity_Discount_Requires_Approval, M2-S04 Opportunity_Products_Required_At_Propose), not a layout backlog. Layout Required binds to that layout only - API, Flow and every other layout ignore it (gotchas #11) - so using it here would look like enforcement and enforce nothing.

decision_record.question: Which behavior does Approval_Status__c carry? (the step's own manual acceptance test, bound against gotchas #11)
decision_record.answer: Readonly. The field is written by the M3 approval process, not by a rep - its own field definition says so ('Set by the discount approval process. Blank means nothing has been submitted for this deal yet') and Q22 makes blank a legal state the process itself produces. A field update sets it regardless of the layout item's behavior, so Readonly costs the approval process nothing and stops a rep typing Approved.
